text:
- [LFCA.10.2] **Catalog is narrow.** Seven capabilities in four categories:
  `actions` (4), `series_capability` (1), `call_modifiers` (1),
  `expression_capability` (1). The deferred storage and samples-plane
  capabilities ([LCAP.2.10]) are not counted.

  Every entry corresponds to something a tier can genuinely lack — a
  runtime capability, or a permission the tier withholds. The two are
  not the same and both are admissible: `series` is gated because
  a tier may have no registered backend, while `cache` is gated because
  a tier may forbid rules from mutating cache state. What is **not**
  admissible is gating something every engine inherently has, which is
  why `cached(...)` is absent ([LFCA.2.4]) and why there is no
  `cache_ttl_arg` — TTL support on an engine-owned cache cannot vary
  by tier.

  Three reasons to gate are legitimate, and they are not all the same
  kind of thing:

  1. **Runtime-subsystem absence.** The tier has no adapters, or no
     series backend — gate off the capabilities that depend on those
     subsystems.
  2. **Latency budget.** The tier cannot afford the round-trip of an
     async `call` — gate off `call` and everything downstream of it.
     This one is neither a capability the tier lacks nor a permission
     it withholds; it is a deployment choice, and it is admissible.
  3. **Tier topology.** The tier is topmost and has nothing to
     `publish` upward to — gate off `publish`.
